tagline.text: Green hills rolling beneath Mayon Volcano in Camalig

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Quitinday, Camalig, Albay, roughly 12 km west of Legazpi

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–1,500 (tricycle charter for a group; per-person environmental fee extra)

children.text: Quitinday Hills is a field of green hills in Camalig, Albay, often compared to Bohol's Chocolate Hills. From the two peaks open to visitors you get a 360-degree view of Mayon Volcano and the surrounding countryside, and the short walk makes it a good half-day trip from Legazpi.
Quitinday Hills sits in Barangay Quitinday in the municipality of Camalig, Albay. Camalig is a small town about
12 km

west of Legazpi with roughly 73,000 residents in the 2024 census, and Quitinday is one of its 50 barangays, home to only 259 people that year. The hill area is described as covering about 400 hectares of rounded green mounds, and the mounds are said to rise about
. They are often likened to Bohol's Chocolate Hills, but pili trees, a Bicol specialty, grow on these hills, so the area is also called the "Pili Nut Hills."
Visitors climb two of the hills. Both peaks open up 360-degree views with an unobstructed look at Mayon Volcano, and a single-track trail joins them, taking about
15 minutes

of gentle walking from the trailhead. A guide is reportedly not required. Mayon is often clear at sunrise and in the late afternoon, which makes those two times popular. Wikivoyage lists the site as the Quitinday Green Hills Formation Reserve, open 24 hours, while another guide says it operates from 5:30 AM to 5:30 PM, so sources differ.

This guide is for travelers staying in Legazpi who feel that Cagsawa Ruins and Daraga Church are not enough. Quitinday Hills is close to the city, but public transport does not reach it directly and you need to hire a tricycle, so it takes a little planning. Combining it with Quitinday Falls and the Underground River, Sumlang Lake and Ligñon Hill makes a full day. Fees and hours come from older or conflicting sources, so check them locally. To visit the falls and the underground river on the same day, start early so the schedule stays comfortable.

Three tips help you enjoy Quitinday Hills. First, Mayon sometimes hides in cloud, so allow at least two days in Legazpi and pick a clear one. Second, a tricycle charter is practically the only way to get around, so tell the driver your return time and, if you can, combine the falls and the underground river to share the cost. Third, there is almost no shade at midday, so plan around sunrise or the late afternoon. This is a small attraction looked after by local people rather than a heavily developed one, so toilets and shops may be fewer than you expect. Buy water and snacks in Camalig town beforehand.
Rounded green hills extend over about 400 hectares and are said to rise about

. The grass can turn golden in the dry season and deep green in the rainy season. The exact number of hills is not known. Between the hills you also see rice paddies, coconut palms and low-roofed houses, giving a taste of village scenery.

Mayon Volcano appears straight ahead from both peaks. Early morning and late afternoon, when there are few clouds, are said to be best. The summit is often covered by cloud, so allow time. Mayon's perfect cone overlaps with the fields below it, which makes good photos, and its color changes with the direction of the setting sun.
The single-track trail linking the two peaks from the trailhead takes about
15 minutes
. The path is gentle enough for children and people who do not exercise much, but there is almost no shelter from the sun, so bring a hat and water.

Pili trees are said to grow among the hills, which gave rise to the nickname "Pili Nut Hills." Pili nuts are a signature Bicol product, so the way back through town is a good time to buy pili sweets or nuts.

You can watch the sun rise behind Mayon Volcano and see the late-afternoon glow. For dawn you need to arrange things with your tricycle driver in advance, and the way down after dark is unlit, so bring a flashlight. In the late afternoon Mayon's ridge often glows red and the clouds clear, which photographers like.

Camping is possible but reportedly needs advance permission. Ask Camalig's tourism office beforehand to confirm the permit and conditions. The starry night sky is a draw. When pitching a tent, avoid windy ridges and bring gear for night temperatures and mosquitoes.
In neighboring Jovellar, Quitinday Falls and the Underground River offer a trip through a cave about
long on a bamboo raft, and tours combine it with the hills. A tricycle tour covering both is said to take about
5–6 hours
From Legazpi, take a jeepney toward Camalig and get off at Quitinday Junction (the diversion road).
Charter a tricycle at the junction to the hill trailhead. One guide says it takes about 45 minutes each way.
Pay the environmental fee at the registration desk and walk the trail to the first peak.
Continue to the second peak and take in Mayon and the fields.
Come down before dark and ride the tricycle back to the junction.
One guide says it closes at 5:30 PM, so if you go late, checking on site is essential. Travel time by jeepney from Legazpi to the junction depends on traffic, so leave with time to spare.

items.subtitle: Quitinday Hills and the underground river

children.text: Leave your hotel by the tricycle you arranged the day before.
Climb the hills and watch the sunrise.
Move on to Quitinday Falls and the Underground River in Jovellar and ride a raft.
Return to Camalig town and have lunch with local food such as pinangat.
Domestic flights run from Manila to Bicol International Airport (DRP) in Daraga. Airlines and schedules change, so check when you book.
From the airport, reach downtown Legazpi by Grab or taxi. Check fares locally.
Camalig lies on the highway (Asian Highway 26) between Legazpi and Daraga, so it is close to the airport.
Long-distance buses run from Manila to Legazpi. They generally travel overnight, so check schedules and travel times with the bus company.
From Legazpi, take a jeepney toward Camalig, Polangui or Guinobatan and get off at Quitinday Junction (the diversion road).
Charter a tricycle at the junction to reach the hills. One guide gives about
round trip for a group of up to five, and about
45 minutes
each way.
To return, catch a jeepney toward Legazpi at the junction. After dark jeepneys may become scarce, so check the last departure locally.
Enter "Quitinday Hills and Nature Park, Camalig, Albay" in a navigation app to be guided to the entrance parking area. Some guides mention a separate parking fee.
Because the point is the hills and Mayon views, the dry season, with little rain and clear skies, is best. During the day, early morning and late afternoon with few clouds are recommended.

In the rainy and typhoon seasons the path is muddy and Mayon is often hidden by cloud. Bicol lies in the path of typhoons, so check the forecast before your trip. At midday there is almost no shade and it gets very hot.

On weekends, local families and photography clubs make the afternoon busier. For a quiet visit, choose an early weekday morning. Operations and fees may change during holidays and events, so check ahead.

Most lodging is in downtown Legazpi rather than Camalig, so it is usual to stay in Legazpi and travel back and forth. To see the sunrise, fix a time with your tricycle driver the day before. Check lodging rates locally. Daraga and Legazpi are both close to Camalig, so for a short trip a hotel near the airport is also an option.

Camalig is famous for pinangat, taro leaves wrapped around meat or shrimp and cooked in coconut milk, and is said to hold a Pinangat Festival in June. Try laing, Bicol Express and pili sweets too. For snacks on the road, pili nut sweets or market fruit are light and easy.
There is almost no shade, so bring plenty of hat, sunscreen and water.
Agreeing on a return time with your tricycle driver makes the trip back after dark easier.
Hours differ by source, so check the closing time before you set out if you go in the late afternoon.
Camping reportedly needs advance permission, so inquire beforehand.
For a sunrise trip, bring a flashlight and a thin jacket.
Take your trash with you.
Quitinday Falls and the Underground River are in a different town, so plan for the longer travel time.
Tricycle fares may need negotiating, so agree before you start on the round trip and waiting time.
The local tourism office is said to explain camping and group-visit conditions if you contact them.
Bicol is exposed to typhoons and Mayon's volcanic activity. Check the volcano alert level and the weather, and follow any restrictions set by the authorities.
After rain the trail is slippery and muddy, so wear non-slip shoes.
There is no shade near the top, so heat exhaustion is a risk at midday.
After sunset the path is dark and quiet. Go with a companion rather than alone.
Quituinan Hills, which has a similar name, is a different place with different fees and operations. Do not confuse them.
Fees and hours come from old or conflicting sources, so check the latest information with Camalig's tourism office or locally before you leave.
The hills may mix private land and public protected areas, so follow signs and staff instructions and keep to the marked path.

These ruins preserve the bell tower of a church buried by the 1814 eruption, and
Cagsawa Ruins
is a place to photograph Mayon Volcano.
This old hilltop church,
Daraga Church
, is fairly close to Camalig and worth combining.

from Camalig.
A small volcanic hill park west of downtown Legazpi that is easy to add to your plans.
